Posts tab scrolled to the end (15 original posts, 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-15); all 15 kept, all are NBA role/usage/minutes/preview notes. Replies tab: the other 3 posts are promo replies on launch day ('Time to work.', 'LFG', 'completely free atm'), dropped.

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Ty Lue challenging Rui Hachimura to average seven or eight rebounds per game this season.

Darius Garland: “He told us with Rui he wants him to average seven or eight rebounds a game.”

(via @TomerAzarly)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Jaden McDaniels expected to average 20-25 points with expanded offensive role.

Anthony Edwards: “Just him getting more touches, being more involved, I think he going to average 20, 25 points easy…just being aggressive, exploiting mixed matches. They try to put the worst defenders on them.”

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Tristan da Silva getting green light to shoot 10-plus threes per game with aggressive role developing.

Sean Sweeney: “That's the most he can take. I mean, that to me is a number for him. … In each of the three preseason games we've had, he's shot over ten threes. And I love the aggressiveness he's showing. He's hunting the right shots. And then defensively, he's done a really good job with his positioning.”

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text: Randle in the Nets first game with everyone in…. 👀

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Julius Randle expected to have the best playmaking season of his career.

Jordi Fernández: “He expects Randle to have the best playmaking season of his career.”

(via @erikslater_)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Yaxel Lendeborg expected to play significant minutes immediately for the Warriors.

Steve Kerr: “As soon as you get a look at his skill, you see his dribble pass shoot skill set. It was obvious, like, yeah, this guy's gonna play a ton for us right away.”

(via @joseph_dycus)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Ja'Kobe Walter projected for 15-20 starts with expanded role in Kawhi Leonard's rest games.

Per @JLew1050: Nobody benefits from Kawhi's rest nights as much as Ja'Kobe will this season. He's probably looking at 15-20 starts and games with an expanded role, and he's a great fit with the first unit on both ends.

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Dillon Brooks expecting more catch-and-shoot looks as Suns stress paint touches and kick-outs.

Dillon Brooks: “I probably get way more now since Miles was on the team with a lot of drives to the rim. A lot of our players are getting paint touches, we're stressing to get to the paint and dish out for an open shot. So I'll probably see more of those.”

(via @DuaneRankin)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Nique Clifford viewed as a secondary ball handler who can play pick-and-roll and facilitate for the Kings.

Doug Christie: “We see him as a secondary ball handler, a guy that can handle the ball, make plays, play in pick-and-roll, a lot of different things. … I think you see them in flashes but you know that what the summertime is for So like you have find your NBA skill you do it at a elite level you work on your complete game but you still do the thing that you do really well... as that thing starts to bud and begins to be something that you can do on the court, you start to see flashes of that, and then it becomes part of your game.”

(via @James_HamNBA)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Bennett Stirtz adjusting to an off-ball role after being the highest-usage player in college basketball.

Mark Daigneault: “He's used to having the ball in his hands. He was like the highest usage player in college basketball last year. And so, moving off the ball is a little new for him. And I think during the weekend, you could see him kind of trying to calibrate the balance of aggression when he's got the ball in his hands and functionality. And today, I thought, was actually his best day... he took the right shots, he attacked on the right plays.”

(via @CAlmanza1007)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Ausar Thompson getting expanded ball-handling reps as the Pistons work to grow his role as a creator.

J.B. Bickerstaff: “We obviously want Ausar to have the ball in his hands. We believe like if he takes a jump, our team is going to take a jump. In order to do that, he's got to get that exposure.”

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
The Clippers plan to build their identity around faster play, cutting and full-court pressure defense.

Ty Lue: “I think we want to be a faster playing team, and we want to be a cutting team. Offensively, not just stand and watch. Defensively, I think we got to get the floor a little bit, try to pick up full court to create turnovers, speed teams up.”

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
The Timberwolves plan to build their offense around the LaMelo Ball and Rudy Gobert pick-and-roll with Ball initiating early.

Chris Finch: “We feel that the LaMelo-Rudy pick-and-roll could have the potential... will be one of the hardest things in the league to guard. So, you know, we need to lean into that.”

(via @DaneMooreNBA)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Ausar Thompson in line for 26-plus minutes with his workload managed in shorter stretches.

J.B. Bickerstaff: “I definitely see his minutes going above 26. … Because we asked him to do so much, how we manage those minutes might look different. Does he run all 10-minute stretches? Maybe, but is he a six-minute here, six-minute, six-minute, you know what I mean?”

(via @HunterPatterson)

posts.author: fcpnba
posts.text:
Yaxel Lendeborg in line for significant minutes as a rookie, whether he starts or comes off the bench.

Steve Kerr: “We're gonna throw him out there whether he's a starter or off the bench. He's going to play a ton and frankly he deserves it. You can see it whether it's summer league or pickup games or now the first couple days of camp. He's one of our best players already. 6'10, 7'4 wingspan. He can dribble, pass and shoot, defend multiple positions. So he's a very important player for us.”

(via @anthonyVslater)
